title: The happiest-looking Stuyvesant band
summary: Blumberg describes the Cuffee, Barker, Kirkpatrick, Braud, Steele lineup as warm, with Braud rebuilding his playing.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: You mentioned the other night about this band that was the happiest looking band that you've seen. At first, yeah.

Yeah, well, these fellas, they all got along perfectly well together. This is with... Who was the trombone? This was Cuffee and Danny Barker and Kirkpatrick on piano and Groh and Steele. And did we say Bushell? Yeah. No, we didn't make it. And Bunk. And they had a very warm thing going. There was very little talk. I mean, there was very little conversation between the musicians, but they all just kind of smiled at each other all night. They all seemed to be enjoying the job very much.
To Steele, the drummer, most of that engagement?
You had mentioned the other night that Groh, which we all know, that Groh hadn't played much for years.

No, he had terrible trouble with his fingers. He was trying to get calluses back. His fingers were bleeding a good deal of the time, but toward the end, I don't remember how many weekends this thing went on, but toward the end, he really started playing strongly and kind of took over the rhythm section at that point. This band actually achieved about the greatest sound of a bunch of guys playing together. Let's get this. Let's get this.
